correctness.rationale: Directly exponentiating the two nilpotent shear perturbations gives \(M_1,M_2\). Multiplication verifies \((M_1^TM_1+M_2^TM_2)/2=qI\) for every shear parameter; conditional expectation and induction establish all-k and all-start second moments. Averaging the matrices gives scalar-times-rotation \(\bar M\) and the stated mean-vector squared-norm law. The full summed generator is damping plus skew-symmetry, so exact deterministic decay holds. The log of q equals \(z(F(z)-2/\beta)\), whose derivative has the sign of \(g(s)=2s/(1+s)-\log(1+s)\) with \(dg/ds=(1-s)/(1+s)^2\); this proves the unique maximum and all boundary cases, including the zero-shear case, ratio equality, and exactly two roots. Exact rational enumeration checked all words up to depth 7 across 4 shear strengths and 3 initial vectors (192 identities); the analytical proof, not finite testing, covers all k/h. The example \(q=3/e>1\) and \(m=2/e<1\) is exact.

value.rationale: The source method is designed to approximate stable dynamics by sparse randomly selected split subsystems; the key practical mathematical gap is whether stable full dynamics and Hurwitz summands suffice for long-time mean-square stability when summands are not dissipative. This complete and sharp two-parameter phase diagram supplies a structural counterexample and benchmark: an explicit unique critical shear/damping ratio, a genuinely reentrant stable–unstable–stable dependence on the grid size, and exact separation of mean-state decay from mean-square explosion. Unlike arbitrary numerical examples or cheap normalization checks, it identifies the natural exact stability boundary of the defining two-generator random time-split model. It does not claim good large-step accuracy or universal control-system performance.
